articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Trabzonspor ve Beşiktaş KAP'a duyurdu: İşte iki kulübün temettü kararı
articles.summaryTr: Trabzonspor ve Beşiktaş, 2025-2026 özel hesap dönemini zararla tamamladı. İki kulübün yönetimi de zarar nedeniyle ortaklara temettü dağıtılmamasına karar verdi.
articles.articleText: Trabzonspor ve Beşiktaş KAP'a duyurdu: İşte iki kulübün temettü kararı - Trabzonspor ve Beşiktaş, 2025-2026 özel hesap dönemini zararla tamamladı. İki kulübün yönetimi de zarar nedeniyle ortaklara temettü dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören Trabzonspor (TSPOR) ve Beşiktaş (BJKAS), 2025-2026 özel hesap dönemine ilişkin kâr dağıtım kararlarını açıkladı. İki kulübün yönetimi de ilgili dönemde oluşan zarar nedeniyle ortaklara kâr payı dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Trabzonspor 1,98 milyar TL zarar açıkladı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Trabzonspor Sportif Yatırım ve Futbol İşletmeciliği, 1 Haziran 2025-31 Mayıs 2026 hesap döneminde Sermaye Piyasası Mevzuatı'na göre 1 milyar 983 milyon 231 bin 658 TL net dönem zararı kaydetti. Şirketin yasal kayıtlarına göre zararı ise 1 milyar 445 milyon 406 bin 18,18 TL olarak açıklandı. Yönetim Kurulu, söz konusu zararın geçmiş yıl zararları hesabında takip edilmesine ve dağıtılacak dönem kârı bulunmaması nedeniyle temettü dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Kararın ilk Olağan Genel Kurul toplantısında ortakların onayına sunulacağı bildirildi. Beşiktaş'ın zararı 1,33 milyar TL Beşiktaş Futbol Yatırımları da 1 Haziran 2025-31 Mayıs 2026 özel hesap dönemini 1 milyar 332 milyon 110 bin 609 TL net dönem zararıyla tamamladı. Şirket tarafından yapılan açıklamada, bağımsız denetimden geçmiş finansal tablolar doğrultusunda kâr dağıtımı yapılmamasına karar verildiği belirtildi. Yönetim Kurulu'nun oybirliğiyle aldığı kararın, ilgili özel hesap dönemine ilişkin Genel Kurul toplantısında pay sahiplerinin onayına sunulacağı ifade edildi. Böylece iki kulübün halka açık şirketleri de 2025-2026 döneminde oluşan zarar nedeniyle yatırımcılarına temettü ödemesi yapmayacak.

articles.title: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
articles.summary: A number of tech figures want the board of the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
articles.summaryTr: A number of tech figures want the board of the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
articles.articleText: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched - Published US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated. Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees. It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion. But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back". The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back. "I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House. The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive. They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process". Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times., external A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report. The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy". Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. 'China plays games with us, so we play games with China' On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China. "They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said. The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping. The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." He added later: "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through." Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. Related topics - Published15 hours ago

The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping. The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." He added later: "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through." Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. articles.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
articles.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
articles.summaryTr: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
articles.articleText: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda - Published Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024. Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest". The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc. In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean. In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda". Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants". He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration". Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants. The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role. "IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms". With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration. Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries. Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. "Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad." The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution. Unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, the agency said. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands". articles.titleTr: Bitcoin'de tasfiye dalgası: Fiyat 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi, kayıp serisi uzadı
articles.summaryTr: Bitcoin, kaldıraçlı pozisyonların peş peşe tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Altı haftadır üst üste değer kaybeden kripto para, pazartesi günü 64 bin dolar seviyesine toparlandı.
articles.articleText: Bitcoin'de tasfiye dalgası: Fiyat 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi, kayıp serisi uzadı - Bitcoin, kaldıraçlı pozisyonların peş peşe tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Altı haftadır üst üste değer kaybeden kripto para, pazartesi günü 64 bin dolar seviyesine toparlandı. Bitcoin, kripto para piyasasında artan satış baskısı ve kaldıraçlı pozisyonların tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda ağustos ayından bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Coin Metrics verilerine göre Bitcoin'in fiyatı cumartesi günü 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Kripto para, pazartesi sabahı ise yeniden 64 bin dolar seviyesine yükseldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Böylece Bitcoin'in haftalık kayıp serisi altı haftaya ulaştı. 1,5 milyar dolara yakın uzun pozisyon tasfiye edildi Bitcoin'deki düşüşte, teknik destek seviyelerinin kırılmasıyla hızlanan zorunlu satışlar etkili oldu. Fiyatın yaklaşık 73 bin dolar seviyesindeki 200 günlük hareketli ortalamanın altına inmesi, kaldıraçlı uzun pozisyonlarda tasfiye dalgasını tetikledi. CoinGlass tarafından takip edilen borsalarda cumartesi gecesi 165 milyon doların üzerinde Bitcoin uzun pozisyonu tasfiye edildi. Bu tutar cuma günü 629 milyon dolar, perşembe günü ise yaklaşık 700 milyon dolar seviyesindeydi. Tasfiyeler, borçlarını kapatmak zorunda kalan yatırımcıların varlıklarını piyasa fiyatından satmasına yol açarak düşüşü hızlandırdı. Güçlü dolar ve kurumsal satış baskısı Bitcoin üzerindeki baskı yalnızca tasfiyelerden kaynaklanmadı. Kasım boyunca güçlü dolar, kurumsal satışlar ve borsa yatırım fonlarına yönelik zayıflayan talep de fiyatı aşağı çekti. ABD dolar endeksi cuma günü Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek seviyesine ulaştı. Beklentilerin üzerinde gelen enflasyon verileri, ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) daha sıkı para politikasını sürdürebileceği beklentilerini güçlendirdi. Dolar ve tahvil getirilerindeki yükseliş, Bitcoin ve altın üzerinde baskı oluşturdu. Ekim sonlarında yapay zeka şirketlerinin değerlemelerine ve harcamalarına ilişkin endişelerle başlayan teknoloji hisselerindeki satışlar da kripto para piyasasındaki düşüşü derinleştirdi. Haberde ayrıca 6,3 milyar dolarlık Binance saldırısı ve kurumsal ETF talebindeki zayıflama da düşüşü artıran faktörler arasında gösterildi. Bitcoin için kritik eşik 60-62 bin dolar Nansen araştırma analisti Nicolai Sondergaard'a göre Bitcoin için 60 bin-62 bin dolar aralığı kritik destek bölgesi konumunda. Sondergaard, Nvidia'nın finansal sonuçlarının teknoloji hisselerindeki satışları artırması durumunda Bitcoin'in 60 bin doların altına inebileceğini belirtti. Analiste göre doların zayıflaması ve reel tahvil getirilerinin düşmesi ise riskli varlıklar üzerindeki baskıyı hafifletebilir. Brickken Üst Yöneticisi Edwin Mata da zorunlu satışların sona ermesinin düşüşü yavaşlatabileceğini, ancak kalıcı bir toparlanma için spot piyasada gerçek alıcıların devreye girmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Analistlere göre Bitcoin'de satış baskısının sona erdiğine ilişkin ilk önemli işaretlerden biri, fiyatın yeniden 73 bin doların üzerine çıkması olacak.

articles.title: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı
articles.summary: ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı
articles.summaryTr: ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi.
articles.articleText: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı - ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. - Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi. ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla mevcut ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek amacıyla yeni bir düzenleme yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlığa bağlı Sanayi ve Güvenlik Bürosu (BIS) tarafından Hazine Bakanlığı ve Ulusal Güvenlik Konseyinin talimatıyla hazırlanan geçici nihai kural, üçüncü ülkelerdeki veri merkezleri üzerinden gelişmiş Amerikan teknolojisine erişimi daha sıkı denetime tabi tutmayı hedefliyor. BIS açıklamasında, bulut bilişim ve yapay zeka altyapısındaki gelişmelerin, ihracat kısıtlamalarına tabi olmayan ülkelerdeki veri merkezleri aracılığıyla gelişmiş çiplere uzaktan erişim imkanı sağladığına dikkat çekildi. Yeni düzenlemenin bu alandaki korumaları mevcut ihracat kontrolleriyle uyumlu hale getireceği belirtildi. 5 ülkeye çip ihracatında lisans şartı Yeni kuralla, ABD'nin savunma ihracatı kısıtlamalarına tabi D:5 Ülke Grubu veya Makao merkezli şirketlere uzaktan yüksek hacimli bilgi işlem kapasitesi sağlayan denizaşırı veri merkezlerine yönelik ihracat, yeniden ihracat ve ülke içi transferlere yeni kısıtlamalar getirildi. Veri merkezleri, yabancı çip üretim tesisleri ve çip ihracatçılarının müşterileri hakkında daha kapsamlı inceleme yapması gerekecek. Bu inceleme, D:5 ülkeleri veya Makao'daki kişi ve kuruluşların doğrudan ya da dolaylı mülkiyet ve kontrol ilişkilerini de kapsayacak. Düzenlemeyle ayrıca Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya gelişmiş çip ihracatı için lisans zorunluluğu getirildi. Ancak belirli raporlama şartlarının karşılanması halinde ABD merkezli şirketlere gönderilecek yarı iletkenler bu zorunluluğun dışında tutulacak. Çevrim içi perakendeciler ve sosyal medya platformlarında kullanılan ticari öneri sistemleri ise ulusal güvenlik açısından aynı riski taşımadıkları gerekçesiyle düzenleme kapsamına alınmadı. İhlallere yaptırım uygulanabilecek ABD yönetimi, düzenlemenin ihlal edilmesine göz yuman ülkeleri de yakından izleyecek. Bu ülkelere yönelik ithalat kısıtlamaları, yeni lisans zorunlulukları ve ihracat yasakları gibi yaptırımlar gündeme gelebilecek. Biden döneminin yapay zeka düzenlemesi kaldırıldı Yeni kural, gelişmiş mantık çiplerinin üretimi ve paketlenmesine ilişkin ihracat kontrollerinde de değişiklikler içeriyor. Böylece yapay zeka çipleri için lisans şartı bulunan ülkelerdeki çip tasarımcılarının mevcut kısıtlamaları aşabileceği yolların daraltılması hedefleniyor. Düzenlemeyle, eski ABD Başkanı Joe Biden döneminde yapay zeka teknolojisinin yayılımını kontrol etmek amacıyla hazırlanan kural da resmen yürürlükten kaldırıldı. Ticaret Bakanlığı, söz konusu düzenlemeyi kaldıracağını Mayıs 2025'te duyurmuştu.

Milyarder yatırımcı Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinden yaklaşık 5,5 milyar dolar değerinde bağışı dört hayırsever vakfa aktardı. Buffett, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda yaptığı bağışın yanı sıra iyilik ve cömertlik üzerine mesajlar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 96 yaşındaki Buffett, 6 bin 150 adet A sınıfı Berkshire Hathaway hissesini 9 milyon 225 bin adet B sınıfı hisseye dönüştürdü. Bu hisselerin 3 milyon 690 binini Susan Thompson Buffett Vakfı'na, 1 milyon 845 binini ise Sherwood Vakfı, Howard G. Buffett Vakfı ve NoVo Vakfı'nın her birine bağışladı. Bağışların ardından Buffett'ın elinde yaklaşık 162 milyar dolar değerinde 182 bin 140 adet A sınıfı hisse kaldı. “İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar” Buffett, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda geçen yılki mesajına atıfta bulunarak iyiliğin değerine dikkat çekti. Ünlü yatırımcı, “Geçen Şükran Günü'nde iyiliğin maliyetsiz ama aynı zamanda paha biçilemez olduğunu yazmıştım. Bir yıl sonra buna yalnızca şunu eklerdim: İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar ve Charlie ile benim satın aldığımız her şeyden daha iyi bir getiri oranına sahiptir” ifadelerini kullandı. Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinin tamamının nihayetinde söz konusu dört vakfa bağışlanacağını yineledi. Bu bağışlarla vakıfların her yıl daha büyük hibeler verebilmesini hedeflediğini belirtti. Berkshire'a güven mesajı Buffett, bağışların yalnızca üç çocuğuna değil, Berkshire Hathaway Üst Yöneticisi Greg Abel'e duyduğu güvenin de bir göstergesi olduğunu söyledi. Üç çocuğunun yıllardır değerli amaçlara yönelik bağışlar yaptığını belirten Buffett, onların yeteneklerine ve bağlılıklarına tamamen güvendiğini ifade etti. Berkshire'a duyduğu güvenin de eylül ayında yaptığı açıklamalardan bu yana değişmediğini vurguladı. Eylül ayında Berkshire Hathaway yönetim kurulu başkanlığı görevini oğlu Howard'a devreden Buffett'ın mektubu, geçen yılki mesajına kıyasla daha kısa oldu. Berkshire Hathaway hisseleri ise dördüncü çeyreğin başından bu yana yüzde 19'dan fazla yükseldi. Şirket hisseleri geçen haftayı art arda dört rekor kapanışla tamamladı. Aynı dönemde S&P 500 endeksi yüzde 1,2 geriledi. Buffett, mektubunu şu tavsiyeyle tamamladı: “Bu Şükran Günü'nde hayatınızdaki özverili insanlardan birine teşekkür edin. Daha da iyisi, başka biri için iyilik yapan kişi olun.”

articles.title: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
articles.summary: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
articles.summaryTr: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
articles.articleText: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs? - Published In Boston, Lincolnshire, a supplier of ready meals to Marks & Spencer (M&S) manufactures thousands of portions of spaghetti bolognese to be sent to the retailer's shops in the Republic of Ireland. Every plastic pallet is meticulously individually tagged with a green-grey label “Eire”. It has been this way since Brexit. Every truck full of food sent to European Union countries requires hundreds of pages of forms, checks by vets, expense and delays. It has cost M&S millions of pounds and is part of that reason the British business shut down 11 French stores in 2021. Many smaller exporters stopped sending their goods to the EU entirely. Some produce, including sausages and certain types of seafood, were entirely stopped. All this was the predictable consequence of former Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s 2020 deal prioritising regulatory freedom over freeflowing goods trade. That will end with a Brexit "reset" that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to sign with the EU on Friday. The government claims it could boost the economy to the tune of £5bn a year and cut the cost of food for households. But will the agreement mean a return to frictionless trade for food with the EU or are there trade-offs and quid pro quos the UK will have to make? EU affairs minister Hamish Falconer, who is a key negotiator with the bloc, acknowledged a “choice” is being made. In exchange for being able to export produce such as Lincolnshire sausages to the 27 countries, the flipside is the extent to which the UK will be able to influence EU food policies. The UK will have a "voice in the room", said Falconer, but no vote. Critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker", not a rule maker. But Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules. Exit clause A Brexit reset would not involve any upfront payments, said Falconer, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment. He said this was "reasonable" to consider what would happen if a future Conservative or Reform government wanted to undo the new arrangements. Both parties have said they would if they were in power. "The EU is worried about that and you can see why," he said. The BBC understands that the clause is a result of EU concerns about the possible cost of having to rebuild facilities for border food safety checks which were put in place following Brexit. The reset means they will be dismantled. The prime minister has said he believes there is a "win-win" deal to be had with the EU. Speaking at a Marks & Spencer food court in central London, Falconer said reducing the cost of importing food "will mean less cost for supermarkets, and I hope that less cost then turns into cheaper produce on the shelves". He said companies have to currently deal with "pages and pages" of form-filling. Some exports are rejected for having the wrong colour of ink on forms, or an inaccurate Latin name for cooked meats. The reset could also mean "tearing up" checks that were introduced on goods flowing from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, following Brexit, he said, as well as separate "Not for EU" labelling. The whole deal to be signed on Friday is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP. Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers' Union, welcomed reduced border inspections and paperwork but said that for the NFU it was "a moment of opportunity and risk" with farmers waiting to see what carve-outs and transitional arrangements would be included. Trade volumes in food exports to the EU had "fallen significantly - by over a third" since 2019, he said. But the UK should take a "pragmatic" approach to implementing any new rules. He raised pesticides and precision breeding - or gene edited crops - as areas where he hoped some compromise would be found. UK firms are, for example, developing tomatoes engineered to contain extra vitamin D. Historically the EU has had much stricter rules on gene-editing, but this year relaxed regulations. Falconer said people would have to "wait and see the detail" in this area. Contentious crisp flavourings Another contentious area has been crisp flavourings, with concerns raised that stricter EU rules on certain ingredients might limit the sale of some popular snack flavours in the UK. "I want to take this opportunity to absolutely stamp down on misinformation about smoky bacon crisps," Falconer said. Post-Brexit the UK had stayed "pretty closely aligned" to European food safety standards, he said. Two leading snack brands had already adapted their recipes to accommodate EU rules, an example of the kind of alignment that would happen whether or not there was a reset of UK-EU relations. "The truth is, almost every business in this country that wants to export food or drink will be aligning with EU rules because it's our biggest market. "Lots of people, like the good people at Walkers and Frazzles have made these changes already, so I would want to reassure people, particularly smoky bacon fans, it's okay," he said. articles.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
articles.summary: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
articles.summaryTr: Russia said Ukraine had launched over 2,000 drones over the course of a day, while Kyiv came under a record 17 air raid alerts.
articles.articleText: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war - Published Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit. The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added. Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people. The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war. The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions. The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences. Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment. Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation. Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children. Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country. Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect. Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member. The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia. The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement. A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US. But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input. "We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov. EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process". articles.title: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
articles.summary: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.

articles.titleTr: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations
articles.summaryTr: British singer Raye lands 11 nominations while Dolly Parton is recognised two months after her death.
articles.articleText: Raye, Rosalía and Dolly Parton recognised in Grammy nominations - Published British singer Raye leads the charge at the forthcoming Grammy Awards with 11 nominations, while Dolly Parton has been recognised with three posthumous nods. Raye is nominated for her latest Mercury-winning record This Album May Contain Hope and its lead single Where Is My Husband!, which is up for both song and record of the year. Other nominees include Rosalía, Ella Langley, Olivia Dean, Ariana Grande, Bruno Mars, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Miranda Lambert and Phoebe Bridgers. Parton's two nominations, both in the best country duo/group performance category, come three months after the country music star died aged 80. Parton is recognised for Butterfly, her collaboration with the Zac Brown Band, and Light of a Clear Blue Morning, alongside an all-star line-up including her goddaughter Miley Cyrus. The late country star also received a nomination for best audio book, for her narration of Star of the Show: My Life on Stage. The Grammy Awards 2027 will take place on Sunday 7 February in Los Angeles. Madonna's album Confessions II, a sequel to 2005's Confessions on a Dancefloor, was absent from the "big four" categories - including album, record and song of the year. That will be seen by many as the Grammys continuing their tradition of snubbing the US singer, but the album did make it into the best dance category. Rosalía's nine nominations for her widely acclaimed album Lux come after her huge success at last week's Latin Grammy Awards. Langley's seven nominations include song of the year for her breakthrough hit Choosin' Texas, which this year became the longest-running number one single in the history of Billboard's Hot 100. There are five new categories being introduced, including best Latin song and best Asian pop music performance. They have been added as part of the Academy's attempts to make the event "more inclusive" and represent a wider range of music genres. However, critics fear that the new specialist categories will result in genres such as K-pop being under-represented in the major categories, and acts including BTS and Stray Kids have said they will boycott next year's ceremony. Four of Korea’s five biggest entertainment companies withheld their music from consideration. Starship Entertainment, which bucked the trend, scored nominations for its girl bands IVE and KiiiKiii. The other nominees were Babymetal, Japanese singer Lisa (not to be confused with the Blackpink star of the same name) and the Filipino bands BINI and SB19. Elsewhere, Beyoncé picked up the 100th nomination of her career when Morning Dew (Donk) was shortlisted for best R&B solo performance. Songs and albums had to be released between 31 August 2025 and 28 August 2026 to qualify for nominations. Around 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy are eligible to vote for the winners. articles.title: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
articles.summary: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack
articles.summaryTr: The Estonian government says Russia was behind the attempted sabotage, which the Kremlin denies.
articles.articleText: Estonia to close Russia border crossings after attempted drone factory arson attack - Published Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory. Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe". The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian. They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids. On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries. The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website. Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia". Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage. The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media. Estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with Russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions. One of them is located at Narva, Estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border. Kremlin spokesman Dimitry Peskov said: "Estonia is building a wall. Many countries, as history demonstrates, have built walls that have brought nothing good to those who erect such walls." Russia has been repeatedly accused by European leaders of targeting national infrastructure and resources destined for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022. Baltic region leaders have repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid attacks and raised fears about the Kremlin's territorial ambitions. Other major backers of Ukraine in Europe, including France, Germany, the UK and Poland, have also said Russia has orchestrated attacks on their soil in recent months. Last year, six men were jailed in the UK over an arson attack linked to Russia at a London warehouse where aid bound for Ukraine was being stored. - Published17 hours ago - Published3 days ago

İki kulübün yönetimi de zarar nedeniyle ortaklara temettü dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören Trabzonspor (TSPOR) ve Beşiktaş (BJKAS), 2025-2026 özel hesap dönemine ilişkin kâr dağıtım kararlarını açıkladı. İki kulübün yönetimi de ilgili dönemde oluşan zarar nedeniyle ortaklara kâr payı dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Trabzonspor 1,98 milyar TL zarar açıkladı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Trabzonspor Sportif Yatırım ve Futbol İşletmeciliği, 1 Haziran 2025-31 Mayıs 2026 hesap döneminde Sermaye Piyasası Mevzuatı'na göre 1 milyar 983 milyon 231 bin 658 TL net dönem zararı kaydetti. Şirketin yasal kayıtlarına göre zararı ise 1 milyar 445 milyon 406 bin 18,18 TL olarak açıklandı. Yönetim Kurulu, söz konusu zararın geçmiş yıl zararları hesabında takip edilmesine ve dağıtılacak dönem kârı bulunmaması nedeniyle temettü dağıtılmamasına karar verdi. Kararın ilk Olağan Genel Kurul toplantısında ortakların onayına sunulacağı bildirildi. Beşiktaş'ın zararı 1,33 milyar TL Beşiktaş Futbol Yatırımları da 1 Haziran 2025-31 Mayıs 2026 özel hesap dönemini 1 milyar 332 milyon 110 bin 609 TL net dönem zararıyla tamamladı. Şirket tarafından yapılan açıklamada, bağımsız denetimden geçmiş finansal tablolar doğrultusunda kâr dağıtımı yapılmamasına karar verildiği belirtildi. Yönetim Kurulu'nun oybirliğiyle aldığı kararın, ilgili özel hesap dönemine ilişkin Genel Kurul toplantısında pay sahiplerinin onayına sunulacağı ifade edildi. Böylece iki kulübün halka açık şirketleri de 2025-2026 döneminde oluşan zarar nedeniyle yatırımcılarına temettü ödemesi yapmayacak.

news.title: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
news.summary: A number of tech figures want the board of the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched
news.summaryTr: A number of tech figures want the board of the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
news.articleText: Trump backs return of ex-Nvidia boss after 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign launched - Published US President Donald Trump has said he "would certainly not mind" seeing Jensen Huang handed back his job as allies of the former Nvidia chief executive called for him to be reinstated. Huang resigned as boss of the AI chip giant last week after the emergence of two affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees. It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms, which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion. But now fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have backed a campaign to get Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back". The pair were among more than 175,000 signatories of an open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted. President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back. "I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House. The president's comments come after the "Stand with Jensen" campaign group, which claims to be made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, demanded the return of the former chief executive. They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process". Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him. The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times., external A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report. The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House. President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal broke out, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy". Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company. The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy. It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions. 'China plays games with us, so we play games with China' On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China. "They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that." he said. The Trump administration issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres on Monday, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models ahead of Trump's meeting with China President Xi Jingping. The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted. Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair. Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said. The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing. The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump. 'A handshake with Jensen' Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation. "Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X., external "Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost." He added later: "If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through." Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm. Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading. In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang". Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation. For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday. Related topics - Published15 hours ago

news.articleText: Borsa İstanbul'da günün yıldızları ve kaybettirenleri belli oldu: İşte o hisseler YAYIN TARİHİ, 16 Kasım 2026 20:04 PAYLAŞ BIST 100 günü yüzde 0,01 düşüşle 11.841,81 puandan tamamladı. Çok sayıda hisse yüzde 10'a yakın yükselirken, bazı hisselerde sert kayıplar yaşandı. İşte günün en çok kazandıran ve kaybettiren hisselerinin tamamı. Borsa İstanbul'da 16 Kasım 2026 Pazartesi günü BIST 100 endeksi yüzde 0,01 düşüşle 11.841,81 puandan kapanış yaptı. Endeksteki sınırlı gerilemeye rağmen çok sayıda hisse günü yüzde 10'a yakın yükselişle tamamladı. Günün en çok kazandıran hisseleri arasında IHLGM, MMCAS, IZFAS, GUNDG, CGCAM, TRHOL ve CITAS yüzde 10 primle ilk sırada yer aldı. En çok kaybettiren hisse ise yüzde 10 düşüş yaşayan ATSYH oldu.

Hem Ukrayna'nın hem de Rusya'nın her ay çok sayıda asker kaybettiğini belirten ABD Başkanı, savaşın insani maliyetine dikkat çekti. Trump ayrıca yakın zamanda Putin ile görüşeceğini söyledi. Ancak görüşmenin tarihi ve gündemine ilişkin ayrıntı paylaşmadı.

news.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
news.summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.

news.titleTr: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
news.summaryTr: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands have announced a "return hub" for failed asylum seekers.
news.articleText: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda - Published Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements. The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin. Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said. The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024. Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest". The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights. The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc. In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean. In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda". Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants". He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration". Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants. The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role. "IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms". With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration. Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries. Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. "Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad." The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution. Unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, the agency said. According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year. In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands". news.summaryTr: Bitcoin, kaldıraçlı pozisyonların peş peşe tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Altı haftadır üst üste değer kaybeden kripto para, pazartesi günü 64 bin dolar seviyesine toparlandı.
news.articleText: Bitcoin'de tasfiye dalgası: Fiyat 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi, kayıp serisi uzadı - Bitcoin, kaldıraçlı pozisyonların peş peşe tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Altı haftadır üst üste değer kaybeden kripto para, pazartesi günü 64 bin dolar seviyesine toparlandı. Bitcoin, kripto para piyasasında artan satış baskısı ve kaldıraçlı pozisyonların tasfiye edilmesiyle hafta sonunda ağustos ayından bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Coin Metrics verilerine göre Bitcoin'in fiyatı cumartesi günü 62 bin dolara kadar geriledi. Kripto para, pazartesi sabahı ise yeniden 64 bin dolar seviyesine yükseldi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Böylece Bitcoin'in haftalık kayıp serisi altı haftaya ulaştı. 1,5 milyar dolara yakın uzun pozisyon tasfiye edildi Bitcoin'deki düşüşte, teknik destek seviyelerinin kırılmasıyla hızlanan zorunlu satışlar etkili oldu. Fiyatın yaklaşık 73 bin dolar seviyesindeki 200 günlük hareketli ortalamanın altına inmesi, kaldıraçlı uzun pozisyonlarda tasfiye dalgasını tetikledi. CoinGlass tarafından takip edilen borsalarda cumartesi gecesi 165 milyon doların üzerinde Bitcoin uzun pozisyonu tasfiye edildi. Bu tutar cuma günü 629 milyon dolar, perşembe günü ise yaklaşık 700 milyon dolar seviyesindeydi. Güçlü dolar ve kurumsal satış baskısı Bitcoin üzerindeki baskı yalnızca tasfiyelerden kaynaklanmadı. Kasım boyunca güçlü dolar, kurumsal satışlar ve borsa yatırım fonlarına yönelik zayıflayan talep de fiyatı aşağı çekti. ABD dolar endeksi cuma günü Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek seviyesine ulaştı. Beklentilerin üzerinde gelen enflasyon verileri, ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) daha sıkı para politikasını sürdürebileceği beklentilerini güçlendirdi. Sondergaard, Nvidia'nın finansal sonuçlarının teknoloji hisselerindeki satışları artırması durumunda Bitcoin'in 60 bin doların altına inebileceğini belirtti. news.title: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı
news.summary: ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı
news.summaryTr: ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi.
news.articleText: ABD'den yapay zeka çiplerine yeni kısıtlama: 5 ülke için lisans şartı - ABD, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek için yeni düzenleme getirdi. - Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya yönelik çip sevkiyatlarında da lisans zorunluluğu genişletildi. ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı, gelişmiş yapay zeka çiplerine ve sunucularına uzaktan erişim yoluyla mevcut ihracat kısıtlamalarının aşılmasını önlemek amacıyla yeni bir düzenleme yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bakanlığa bağlı Sanayi ve Güvenlik Bürosu (BIS) tarafından Hazine Bakanlığı ve Ulusal Güvenlik Konseyinin talimatıyla hazırlanan geçici nihai kural, üçüncü ülkelerdeki veri merkezleri üzerinden gelişmiş Amerikan teknolojisine erişimi daha sıkı denetime tabi tutmayı hedefliyor. BIS açıklamasında, bulut bilişim ve yapay zeka altyapısındaki gelişmelerin, ihracat kısıtlamalarına tabi olmayan ülkelerdeki veri merkezleri aracılığıyla gelişmiş çiplere uzaktan erişim imkanı sağladığına dikkat çekildi. Yeni düzenlemenin bu alandaki korumaları mevcut ihracat kontrolleriyle uyumlu hale getireceği belirtildi. 5 ülkeye çip ihracatında lisans şartı Yeni kuralla, ABD'nin savunma ihracatı kısıtlamalarına tabi D:5 Ülke Grubu veya Makao merkezli şirketlere uzaktan yüksek hacimli bilgi işlem kapasitesi sağlayan denizaşırı veri merkezlerine yönelik ihracat, yeniden ihracat ve ülke içi transferlere yeni kısıtlamalar getirildi. Veri merkezleri, yabancı çip üretim tesisleri ve çip ihracatçılarının müşterileri hakkında daha kapsamlı inceleme yapması gerekecek. Bu inceleme, D:5 ülkeleri veya Makao'daki kişi ve kuruluşların doğrudan ya da dolaylı mülkiyet ve kontrol ilişkilerini de kapsayacak. Düzenlemeyle ayrıca Endonezya, Malezya, Singapur, Tayland ve Brezilya'ya gelişmiş çip ihracatı için lisans zorunluluğu getirildi. Ancak belirli raporlama şartlarının karşılanması halinde ABD merkezli şirketlere gönderilecek yarı iletkenler bu zorunluluğun dışında tutulacak. Çevrim içi perakendeciler ve sosyal medya platformlarında kullanılan ticari öneri sistemleri ise ulusal güvenlik açısından aynı riski taşımadıkları gerekçesiyle düzenleme kapsamına alınmadı. İhlallere yaptırım uygulanabilecek ABD yönetimi, düzenlemenin ihlal edilmesine göz yuman ülkeleri de yakından izleyecek. Bu ülkelere yönelik ithalat kısıtlamaları, yeni lisans zorunlulukları ve ihracat yasakları gibi yaptırımlar gündeme gelebilecek. Biden döneminin yapay zeka düzenlemesi kaldırıldı Yeni kural, gelişmiş mantık çiplerinin üretimi ve paketlenmesine ilişkin ihracat kontrollerinde de değişiklikler içeriyor. Böylece yapay zeka çipleri için lisans şartı bulunan ülkelerdeki çip tasarımcılarının mevcut kısıtlamaları aşabileceği yolların daraltılması hedefleniyor. Düzenlemeyle, eski ABD Başkanı Joe Biden döneminde yapay zeka teknolojisinin yayılımını kontrol etmek amacıyla hazırlanan kural da resmen yürürlükten kaldırıldı. Ticaret Bakanlığı, söz konusu düzenlemeyi kaldıracağını Mayıs 2025'te duyurmuştu.

news.titleTr: Ünlü milyarder Warren Buffett'tan 5,5 milyar dolarlık bağış: “İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar”
news.summaryTr: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinden yaklaşık 5,5 milyar dolarlık bağışı dört vakfa aktardı. 96 yaşındaki milyarder, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda iyiliğin de bileşik getiri sağladığını vurguladı.
news.articleText: Ünlü milyarder Warren Buffett'tan 5,5 milyar dolarlık bağış: “İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar” - Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinden yaklaşık 5,5 milyar dolarlık bağışı dört vakfa aktardı. 96 yaşındaki milyarder, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda iyiliğin de bileşik getiri sağladığını vurguladı. Milyarder yatırımcı Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinden yaklaşık 5,5 milyar dolar değerinde bağışı dört hayırsever vakfa aktardı. Buffett, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda yaptığı bağışın yanı sıra iyilik ve cömertlik üzerine mesajlar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 96 yaşındaki Buffett, 6 bin 150 adet A sınıfı Berkshire Hathaway hissesini 9 milyon 225 bin adet B sınıfı hisseye dönüştürdü. Bu hisselerin 3 milyon 690 binini Susan Thompson Buffett Vakfı'na, 1 milyon 845 binini ise Sherwood Vakfı, Howard G. Buffett Vakfı ve NoVo Vakfı'nın her birine bağışladı. Bağışların ardından Buffett'ın elinde yaklaşık 162 milyar dolar değerinde 182 bin 140 adet A sınıfı hisse kaldı. “İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar” Buffett, yıllık Şükran Günü mektubunda geçen yılki mesajına atıfta bulunarak iyiliğin değerine dikkat çekti. Ünlü yatırımcı, “Geçen Şükran Günü'nde iyiliğin maliyetsiz ama aynı zamanda paha biçilemez olduğunu yazmıştım. Bir yıl sonra buna yalnızca şunu eklerdim: İyilik bileşik getiri sağlar ve Charlie ile benim satın aldığımız her şeyden daha iyi bir getiri oranına sahiptir” ifadelerini kullandı. Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway hisselerinin tamamının nihayetinde söz konusu dört vakfa bağışlanacağını yineledi. Bu bağışlarla vakıfların her yıl daha büyük hibeler verebilmesini hedeflediğini belirtti. Berkshire'a güven mesajı Buffett, bağışların yalnızca üç çocuğuna değil, Berkshire Hathaway Üst Yöneticisi Greg Abel'e duyduğu güvenin de bir göstergesi olduğunu söyledi. Üç çocuğunun yıllardır değerli amaçlara yönelik bağışlar yaptığını belirten Buffett, onların yeteneklerine ve bağlılıklarına tamamen güvendiğini ifade etti. Berkshire'a duyduğu güvenin de eylül ayında yaptığı açıklamalardan bu yana değişmediğini vurguladı. Eylül ayında Berkshire Hathaway yönetim kurulu başkanlığı görevini oğlu Howard'a devreden Buffett'ın mektubu, geçen yılki mesajına kıyasla daha kısa oldu. Berkshire Hathaway hisseleri ise dördüncü çeyreğin başından bu yana yüzde 19'dan fazla yükseldi. Şirket hisseleri geçen haftayı art arda dört rekor kapanışla tamamladı. Aynı dönemde S&P 500 endeksi yüzde 1,2 geriledi. Buffett, mektubunu şu tavsiyeyle tamamladı: “Bu Şükran Günü'nde hayatınızdaki özverili insanlardan birine teşekkür edin. Daha da iyisi, başka biri için iyilik yapan kişi olun.”

Üç çocuğunun yıllardır değerli amaçlara yönelik bağışlar yaptığını belirten Buffett, onların yeteneklerine ve bağlılıklarına tamamen güvendiğini ifade etti. Berkshire'a duyduğu güvenin de eylül ayında yaptığı açıklamalardan bu yana değişmediğini vurguladı. Eylül ayında Berkshire Hathaway yönetim kurulu başkanlığı görevini oğlu Howard'a devreden Buffett'ın mektubu, geçen yılki mesajına kıyasla daha kısa oldu. Berkshire Hathaway hisseleri ise dördüncü çeyreğin başından bu yana yüzde 19'dan fazla yükseldi. Şirket hisseleri geçen haftayı art arda dört rekor kapanışla tamamladı. Aynı dönemde S&P 500 endeksi yüzde 1,2 geriledi. Buffett, mektubunu şu tavsiyeyle tamamladı: “Bu Şükran Günü'nde hayatınızdaki özverili insanlardan birine teşekkür edin. Daha da iyisi, başka biri için iyilik yapan kişi olun.”

news.title: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
news.summary: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
news.summaryTr: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
news.articleText: Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs? - Published In Boston, Lincolnshire, a supplier of ready meals to Marks & Spencer (M&S) manufactures thousands of portions of spaghetti bolognese to be sent to the retailer's shops in the Republic of Ireland. Every plastic pallet is meticulously individually tagged with a green-grey label “Eire”. It has been this way since Brexit. Every truck full of food sent to European Union countries requires hundreds of pages of forms, checks by vets, expense and delays. It has cost M&S millions of pounds and is part of that reason the British business shut down 11 French stores in 2021. Many smaller exporters stopped sending their goods to the EU entirely. Some produce, including sausages and certain types of seafood, were entirely stopped. All this was the predictable consequence of former Prime Minister Boris Johnson’s 2020 deal prioritising regulatory freedom over freeflowing goods trade. That will end with a Brexit "reset" that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to sign with the EU on Friday. The government claims it could boost the economy to the tune of £5bn a year and cut the cost of food for households. But will the agreement mean a return to frictionless trade for food with the EU or are there trade-offs and quid pro quos the UK will have to make? EU affairs minister Hamish Falconer, who is a key negotiator with the bloc, acknowledged a “choice” is being made. In exchange for being able to export produce such as Lincolnshire sausages to the 27 countries, the flipside is the extent to which the UK will be able to influence EU food policies. The UK will have a "voice in the room", said Falconer, but no vote. Critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker", not a rule maker. But Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules. Exit clause A Brexit reset would not involve any upfront payments, said Falconer, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment. He said this was "reasonable" to consider what would happen if a future Conservative or Reform government wanted to undo the new arrangements. Both parties have said they would if they were in power. "The EU is worried about that and you can see why," he said. The BBC understands that the clause is a result of EU concerns about the possible cost of having to rebuild facilities for border food safety checks which were put in place following Brexit. The reset means they will be dismantled. The prime minister has said he believes there is a "win-win" deal to be had with the EU. Speaking at a Marks & Spencer food court in central London, Falconer said reducing the cost of importing food "will mean less cost for supermarkets, and I hope that less cost then turns into cheaper produce on the shelves". He said companies have to currently deal with "pages and pages" of form-filling. Some exports are rejected for having the wrong colour of ink on forms, or an inaccurate Latin name for cooked meats. The reset could also mean "tearing up" checks that were introduced on goods flowing from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, following Brexit, he said, as well as separate "Not for EU" labelling. The whole deal to be signed on Friday is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP. Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers' Union, welcomed reduced border inspections and paperwork but said that for the NFU it was "a moment of opportunity and risk" with farmers waiting to see what carve-outs and transitional arrangements would be included. Trade volumes in food exports to the EU had "fallen significantly - by over a third" since 2019, he said. But the UK should take a "pragmatic" approach to implementing any new rules. He raised pesticides and precision breeding - or gene edited crops - as areas where he hoped some compromise would be found. UK firms are, for example, developing tomatoes engineered to contain extra vitamin D. Historically the EU has had much stricter rules on gene-editing, but this year relaxed regulations. Falconer said people would have to "wait and see the detail" in this area. Contentious crisp flavourings Another contentious area has been crisp flavourings, with concerns raised that stricter EU rules on certain ingredients might limit the sale of some popular snack flavours in the UK. "I want to take this opportunity to absolutely stamp down on misinformation about smoky bacon crisps," Falconer said. Post-Brexit the UK had stayed "pretty closely aligned" to European food safety standards, he said. Two leading snack brands had already adapted their recipes to accommodate EU rules, an example of the kind of alignment that would happen whether or not there was a reset of UK-EU relations. "The truth is, almost every business in this country that wants to export food or drink will be aligning with EU rules because it's our biggest market. "Lots of people, like the good people at Walkers and Frazzles have made these changes already, so I would want to reassure people, particularly smoky bacon fans, it's okay," he said. news.articleText: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war - Published Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit. The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added. Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people. The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war. The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions. The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences. Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment. Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation. Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children. Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country. Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect. Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member. The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia. The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement. A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US. But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input. "We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov. EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process". The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added. Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people. The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war. The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions. The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences. Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment. Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation. Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children. Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country. Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect. Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member. The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia. The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement. A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US. But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input. "We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov. EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".
